vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-tasks
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle provides a standard interface for managing Google Tasks via the 'gws' CLI tool. The documentation in SKILL.md correctly outlines CRUD operations for tasks and task lists without any evidence of malicious intent, unauthorized data access, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's actions (calling a 'gws' CLI to manage Google Tasks) match its description, but it defers authentication and security rules to an external shared SKILL.md file (../gws-shared/SKILL.md) that is not declared or included — this external dependency and unspecified auth are unexpected and worth inspection before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Google Tasks) align with the runtime instructions which call the 'gws' CLI to manage tasklists and tasks. Requiring the 'gws' binary is proportionate for a CLI-based Google Tasks helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules — this directs the agent to load configuration or credentials from a sibling path outside the skill bundle. If that file is missing it tells the agent to run 'gws generate-skills', which may create files. This external-file dependency is not included in the skill metadata and could expose or rely on secrets/configuration not declared here.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec; nothing is written to disk by the skill itself. Lowest-risk install profile, provided the referenced 'gws' binary is trusted and already present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, but it depends on external auth via the shared SKILL.md or the 'gws' CLI's own auth. That means credentials (OAuth tokens, gcloud creds, or other secrets) will likely be used at runtime even though they are not declared here — the absence of explicit credential requirements reduces transparency.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install behavior in the skill metadata. The skill does not request system-wide persistence or modifications to other skills' configs in its instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose (it shells out to a 'gws' CLI to manage Google Tasks) but relies on an external shared SKILL.md for authentication and security rules that is not included or declared. Before installing: 1) Inspect the ../gws-shared/SKILL.md referenced by this skill (or ask the publisher for it) to see what credentials or config it contains. 2) Verify the provenance of the 'gws' binary on your system (where it came from, what account it will access, and how it authenticates — OAuth token files, gcloud credentials, service account keys, etc.). 3) Do not run 'gws generate-skills' or other generator commands unless you trust the source; they may create files or config. 4) Ensure least-privilege: limit which Google account or OAuth scopes the CLI can use. 5) If you cannot inspect the shared SKILL.md or confirm how 'gws' authenticates, treat this skill as potentially unsafe and avoid installing it.
